# vachaka


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

vachaka turns Devanagari into recited audio and tells you where every
line and word falls in it. It is a thin layer over two models by
Prathosh A. P.: [Vāgdhenu](https://github.com/prathoshap/vagdhenu), a
metre-aware chant TTS (an IndicF5 fine-tune with a BigVGAN-v2 vocoder),
and [Su-śrotā](https://huggingface.co/prathoshap/sushrota-sanskrit-asr),
a Sanskrit ASR (IndicConformer fine-tuned on śāstric Sanskrit). Vāgdhenu
does the speaking. Su-śrotā listens back: it scores each render against
its text, so a bad seed can be thrown away, and it force-aligns the
words.

It was written for [VedicReader](https://vedicreader.com), which has
thousands of Sanskrit verses and sūtras with no recording. The input
there is a title’s display lines, and the output has to be one audio
file plus a `[start, end]` for every line and word, so the reader can
follow along. That is what `vachaka.recite` does.

## Listen

Clips from a pilot run over VedicReader’s texts. The voice is synthetic,
and it is Vāgdhenu’s author’s. CER is Su-śrotā’s character error rate
for the clip against its text. The players work on the [docs

the text.

At that speed an hour of recitation takes five to six hours on a laptop.
A CUDA GPU is much faster; Vāgdhenu’s author renders on one.

Two cautions. Su-śrotā comes from the same lab and its training data
includes a TTS-speaker slice, so it may hear Vāgdhenu more kindly than a
person would; a low CER says the words are there, not that the chant is
beautiful. And a section whose metre is not detected (āryā, a verse
split over three lines) is read as prose, which sounds flatter than a
chant. Listen before you ship.

## Install

``` sh
pip install vachaka            # rendering
pip install 'vachaka[check]'   # Su-śrotā: transcripts, error rate, word timings
```

Python 3.10 to 3.12. The first
[`Chanter()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vachaka/core.html#chanter)
downloads about 1.5 GB of weights from the Hugging Face Hub and fetches
the sources of Vāgdhenu, BigVGAN and IndicF5 at pinned commits into
`~/.cache/vachaka` (set `VACHAKA_CACHE` to move it); none of the three
is on PyPI, and the `f5-tts` that is differs from IndicF5. Su-śrotā is
520 MB more. Writing mp3 needs `ffmpeg`.

## Use

Chant a verse given as its lines, and read prose:

``` python
from vachaka.core import Chanter
ch = Chanter()                        # cuda, then mps, then cpu
r = ch.chant(['वसुदेवसुतं देवं कंसचाणूरमर्दनम्', 'देवकीपरमानन्दं कृष्णं वन्दे जगद्गुरुम्'])
r.spans                               # [(0, 4230), (4980, 9550)]: one span per line, in ms
r.save('krishna.mp3')
ch.read('अथातो धर्मजिज्ञासा । चोदनालक्षणोऽर्थो धर्मः ।', ref='anuṣṭubh').save('mimamsa.mp3')
```

Check a render and time its words:

``` python
from vachaka.check import Ear, best_of
ear = Ear()
lines = ['वसुदेवसुतं देवं कंसचाणूरमर्दनम्', 'देवकीपरमानन्दं कृष्णं वन्दे जगद्गुरुम्']
r = best_of(lambda seed: ch.chant(lines, seed=seed), ear, ' '.join(lines))
r.cer                                 # 0.0
ear.hear(r.audio, r.sr)               # 'वसुदेवसुतं देवं कंसचाणूरमर्दनं देवकीपरमानन्दं कृष्णं वन्दे जगद्गुरुं'
ear.words(r, [l.split() for l in lines])
# [[['वसुदेवसुतं', 120, 1279], ['देवं', 1279, 1878], ['कंसचाणूरमर्दनम्', 1878, 3756]],
#  [['देवकीपरमानन्दं', 5100, 7018], ['कृष्णं', 7018, 7697], ['वन्दे', 7697, 8217], ['जगद्गुरुम्', 8217, 9056]]]
```

Recite whole sections from their display lines, with daṇḍas, verse
numbers and accents left in; each line comes back with its span and
words:

``` python
from vachaka.recite import recite
rec, info = recite(ch, ear, [dict(lines=['नित्यानन्दकरी वराभयकरी सौन्दर्यरत्नाकरी', 'निर्धूताखिलघोरपावनकरी प्रत्यक्षमाहेश्वरी ।',
                                         'प्रालेयाचलवंशपावनकरी काशीपुराधीश्वरी', 'भिक्षां देहि कृपावलम्बनकरी मातान्नपूर्णेश्वरी ॥ १ ॥'])])
info[0]['kind'], info[0]['ref'], info[0]['lines'][0]   # 'chant', 'shardulavikridita', {'s': ..., 'e': ..., 'w': [...]}
```

For batches there is a resumable CLI over jsonl:
`vachaka-recite jobs.jsonl results.jsonl`, where a job is
`dict(id, out, sections)`.

## How it works

[`recite`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vachaka/recite.html#recite)
groups display lines into pieces, closing a piece after a daṇḍa, so the
two pādas of a hemistich printed on two lines render together, as
Vāgdhenu expects. Each verse (closing on a double daṇḍa) is scanned by
[ganapati](https://github.com/vedicreader/ganapati): one in a metre from
Vāgdhenu’s bank is chanted against that metre’s reference clip, another
vṛtta against vasantatilakā, and an āryā or anything that does not scan
is read in chunks of at most 24 akṣaras. So a commentary that quotes a
verse chants the verse and reads the rest. Vāgdhenu renders each piece
separately and joins them with short silences; vachaka records where
each piece landed. Su-śrotā then transcribes the whole render, and if
the error rate is above 8% the section is rendered again with another
seed, keeping the best of three. Finally the words of each piece are
force-aligned (torchaudio’s CTC aligner on Su-śrotā’s posteriors) inside
that piece’s span, so one bad line can’t pull the rest out of place.

Two things had to be patched to run this on a Mac. BigVGAN’s transposed
convolution has more than 65,536 output channels, which MPS rejects, so
the vocoder runs on the CPU. And Su-śrotā’s checkpoint names AI4Bharat’s
NeMo fork; vachaka rewrites its config for upstream NeMo (the tokenizer
type becomes `agg`, the fork’s `multisoftmax` keys go) and uses only the
encoder and the CTC head, the Sanskrit columns 4096 to 4351.

## Limits

No Vedic svaras: Vāgdhenu is laukika chant, and accents are stripped
before rendering. One voice, the model author’s. The reference clip sets
pace and melody but not timbre. Metres outside Vāgdhenu’s bank fall back
to vasantatilakā when detected as some other vṛtta, and to prose when
not detected at all. Prose sounds like careful reading, not chant.
